pages.name: Finding a Patron
pages.html:
A main drive for a spacer is to survive in the far future by taking on odd jobs to scrape by as they travel around. The following section helps outline finding jobs by generating patrons and their employment opportunities.

Finding a Patron: When a spacer is seeking a patron, they must make it known in areas where they are seeking their ideal clientele. Different locations will attract a different clientele. To generate the type of patron available in a location, use the table range listed below to determine what die is rolled on the Patron Table, listed in the parentheses, and which range of results it is rolled on.

  • For example: D3-1, 1D means roll a D3-1 for the tens place and 1D means roll 1D for the ones place when rolling on the Patron D66 table.

pages.name: Patron Job Generation
pages.html:
Patron Job Generation: Use the following to determine the type of job the patron is offering.

  • Type of Job: Roll 1D to determine what Type of job the spacers are being scouted for, then roll 2D to determine the job description and details.
  • Payment: The listed payment for each is multiplied by the total amount of time the patron sets to complete the job; see Negotiate Job table. Note: Enrichment jobs use their described payment amounts.
  • Develop a Narrative: Using the generated gig objective, use the patron’s type to determine the narrative hook of the gig.
  • Optional—Number of objectives: Each job will typically be the single objective. However, if the spacers would like to take on more of a challenge, they may have up to 3 objectives to complete at the patron’s request. Roll a D3 then roll that many times on the table below to determine each objective.

Scenario Types

  • Chase/Pursuit: This type of job has the spacer attempt to find the objective of the job, but the roles may flip if a complication occurs.
    • Payment: 1D x 500cr x max weeks to complete.
  • Assault/Rescue: This job assumes that the spacer is willing to engage in violence to complete the job. If a complication occurs, then the focus/target of the job is not what it seems or they weren’t informed fully about it.
    • Payment: 1D x 1000cr x max weeks to complete.
  • Discovery/Exploration: The spacer doing a job of this type is expected to expertly find accurate information and survive in whatever location they are expected to collect data from. A complication that occurs will reveal an unexpected (and possibly dangerous) outcome for completing the job.
    • Payment: 1D+6 x 1000cr x max weeks to complete.
  • Enrichment: Enrichment jobs are short term (and potentially high risk) payouts transporting or recovering people, trade goods, or similar. Typically a patron asking the spacers to do this is employing them to do the job because they cannot do it themselves or do not want to risk doing it themselves. A complication that occurs is that the subject of the job is not what it seems and could lead to further trouble.
    • For Payment, see Enrichment Job Table below.
  • Enigma/Mystery: The spacers are hired to help figure out a mystery, to try to find answers for the patron. Complications may include that learning the answers results in understanding why the enigma wasn’t answered before, due to a lingering threat.
    • Payment: 2D x 2000cr x max weeks to complete.
  • Novelty: A novelty job is a unique employment opportunity that is normally not encountered or expected. Complications can result in role reversals, unexpected dangers and stressful situations.
    • Payment: 2D+3 x 2000cr x max weeks to complete.

Job Payment Amount: The listed payment for a job is for the spacers only. If they have crew members, they are expected to pay their crew their expected amount.

  • Per Week Payment: Payment for a job will be in weeks if the spacers are located in one planetary area or in one star system. Payment does not cover the cost of travelling to the job location if the job will take longer than it takes to travel there.
  • Patron Payment Multiplier: Apply the payment multiplier from the Find a Patron table to determine any changes in the total job payment.

pages.name: Job Negotiations
pages.html:
Patron Job Negotiation: Use the following procedure to determine a patron's demeanor, the terms of the job, the payment, and when to start the job.

  • Patron Demeanor: Use the NPC Demeanor Table (pg.56) to determine how the patron responds to the spacers and apply any DM the table dictates. This represents how the patron comes off when dealing with a group of spacers, based on the patron’s perception of them.
  • Negotiate Terms: Apply the SOC DM for the negotiating spacer to the roll on this table. The 2D result is used for both columns. Remember, the generated final payment is multiplied by the total amount of weeks assigned for job completion.

pages.name: Job Destination and Assumptions
pages.html:

  • Payment: It is assumed that there will be a means of payment upon arrival if the job sends the spacer to a location without a starport or settlement.

Settlement: Roll 1D to determine the type of settlement: 1-3) Planetside 4-5) Moon/Asteroid 6) Orbital Space Station.

  • Distance from Starport: Roll 1D to determine if the settlement is near the starport.
  • Result 1-3: The settlement is close to a major starport or has one locally.
  • Result of 4-5: The settlement is 1D x 100km away from the nearest starport. Either risk landing on the local terrain or dock at the starport and take a terrestrial vehicle to the settlement.
  • Result of 6+: The settlement is 2D x 100km away from the nearest starport.

Book p.54
